note: ADR-0011 3.2 and 3.5; bars set from the first measured run (see the PR). The curves are stated functions, not circuits, so the reference is their own Fourier series, computed in double by the suite: the output's harmonics 2-9 of a 1 kHz tone (standard, three levels, every shape, at 44.1, 48 and 96 kHz) within harmonics.db of it wherever the reference stands above harmonics.floor_dbc; the exciter's added harmonics of a 3 kHz tone against the series at the level the split passes (the split's exact one-pole response); the tone shelf against its analytic first-order response. Small-signal gain is unity at every drive, shape and frequency (the drive is divided out). Aliasing is non-harmonic energy on tones from 1 to 19 kHz. Nominal (drive 12 dB, -18 dBFS): standard and high meet ADR-0011's -90 dBc over the whole sweep; eco meets its -70 dBc to 8 kHz, and above it a 2x oversampler folds the 4th and 5th harmonics of 10-19 kHz tones into the band (measured -66.5 dBc soft, -53.7 dBc warm at 44.1 kHz), held to the ceiling aliasing.nominal.eco_all_dbc and reported. Hot (drive 18 dB, -6 dBFS, tones to 8 kHz): per shape and quality, at the figures measured at 44.1 kHz (the worst rate) plus 2 dB; the 36 dB drive level is reported. Aliasing at a heavy drive is the curve's own: hard clipping aliases most, which is why high (8x) exists. The zipper tone is -40 dBFS, so full drive stays clean enough that the harmonics are not read as steps; the bar moves with it (checks.cpp). Hot input: squares at 0, +12 and +24 dBFS, drive 36 dB, every shape and mode, finite and bounded (the exciter's bound carries the oversampler's Gibbs ringing on the replaced high band). CPU: eco is held to class B on the programme and on the +12 dB / drive 36 dB / exciter worst case; standard and high are reported, over it (their 4x and 8x oversamplers alone take most of the budget), as ADR-0011 3.5 allows beside an eco that meets it.
